summary: Nancy Hatch Dupree worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Barnard College (~1945–1949) and Columbia University (~1950–1952), and held a post at Kabul University from circa 2006 to 2017.

Nancy Hock specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at UC Berkeley in 1987 under Joanna Gottfried Williams, Lewis Lancaster, Eugene F. Irschick, and Barend A. van Nooten, and was affiliated with the Asian Art Museum in 1987.

Nancy McCagney specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, Gerald James Larson, William F. Powell, and Andrew Rawlinson, and held a post at the University of Delaware in 1997.

Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She served as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research and as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies in 2011.
Nang Dzé Drubpé Dorjé studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Nanigopal Majumdar was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He served as Superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India in 1931 and as Superintendent of the Archaeological Section at the Indian Museum, Kolkata, attested in 1939.
Nantu Shaw works in philosophy and Indology. In 2026, he was a visiting scholar at Stony Brook University, studying under doctoral supervisor Sthaneshwar Timalsina.

Naoji Okuyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1980–1985), where he worked from ~1985 to 1993, and became a professor at Koyasan University around 1999.
Naoki Nabeshima is a Buddhist studies scholar who founded and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Ryukoku University (attested 2004).

Naoko Nishimura specializes in Indology and linguistics. She completed her PhD at Tohoku University (1993–2002), studying under Toshifumi Goto, Hirofumi Isoda, and Shinkan Murakami, and was a specialist researcher there as of 2026.

Naomi Appleton works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. at Oxford under Christopher Minkowski and David Gellner, held a fellowship at Cardiff University, and has held professorial and teaching posts at the University of Edinburgh.
Naomi Worth specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Virginia and held a post there in 2018.
Naomichi Nakada is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under doctoral supervisor Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale and under Ram Chandra Pandeya.

Naoshiro Tsuji was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Oxford. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1942–1960), professor at Keio University, and director of Toyo Bunko.
Naoya Funahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science and at Otani University (attested 1981).

Narada Maha Thera was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure. Educated at St. Benedict's College and University College in Colombo, he served as Superior of Vajiraramaya Temple from circa 1955 to 1983.

Narayan Hemandas Samtani specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Delhi (1957–1961) under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale, and served as a Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University (~1961–1984).
Narayana Shastri Khiste was an Indologist who served as Librarian at the Sarasvati Bhavana Library (attested 1932) and as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1950).
Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya was a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology who held a post at the University of Calcutta from circa 1967 to 1999.
Narendrachandra Bhattacharyya worked in Indology and philosophy. He was General Editor of the Calcutta Sanskrit Series (attested 1936) and a Pandit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1943).
